newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dlr inches higher, but market mood sober.
newsitem.headline: Australia dlr inches higher, but market mood sober.

text.p: The Australian dollar crept higher at the midsession in relief the Reserve Bank passed up another opportunity to cut rates but shied away from testing rumoured offshore offers around US$0.7550 resistance.
Sentiment was tugged two ways as Moody's revised the outlook for a number of Australian states to positive, but a NAB survey showed business conditions were mixed at best in Q2.

The currency was bought against the Kiwi on the view rates here were on hold for now, while conditions had eased further in New Zealand since the RBNZ sanctioned a move last week. Indeed, the RBNZ protested the extent of the easing this morning.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the local dollar was idling at US$0.7530/35 after crawling up from US$0.7515/20 late Wednesday.
It did stretch as far as US$0.7553 overnight as speculators went hunting for stop loss orders but lapsed when they met heavy offers instead.

Some of the latter were rumoured to originate from Asian bank protecting a strangle option and dealers, while always sceptical of such talk, were not keen to test its veracity buy chasing the currency higher.
Support was expected at US$0.7505 and there were further bulwarks at US$0.7470 and US$0.7440, this week's low.

The Federal Reserve's decision to leave U.S. rates unchanged after its policy meeting Wednesday surprised no one and actually had an adverse effect on the A$ at first since the market assumed it opened a window of opportunity for the RBA to ease.
If so, it was one the bank did not take, which supported the bank's oft-stated position that monetary policy was ruled by domestic factors.

Most analysts continue to believe these factors argue for another easing with underlying inflation heading under the RBA's 2-3 percent target band, economic growth running well below potential and unemployment stuck at unacceptably high levels.

Many expect the case to be reinforced by three major upcoming releases, being employment data for June are released on July 10, the Q2 consumer price index on July 23 and key wages data the day after.
If all are as subdued as the easing camp expect, the RBA could well move on July 25 or after its next board meeting on August 5.

The prospect was not a promising one for A$ bulls and few thought the currency could sustain a rally above US$0.7570, no matter US$0.7630 resistance, until the market was certain the year-old Australian easing cycle had ended.
On the crosses the dollar shifted up to NZ$1.1130/48 from NZ$1.1081/96 late here Wednesday and a low of 1.0820 just a couple of weeks ago.

The Kiwi has been losing ground since the RBNZ endorsed an easing last week which was then extended by the market after soft GDP data. The central bank protested the additional loosening this morning but so far with little effect on the NZ$.

The local dollar was a shade easier on the yen at 86.14/24 from 86.40/50 but steady in trade weighted terms at 57.6. It remained sharply higher at around 22.00 baht after the Thai currency was floated Wednesday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
